title: Misrouted metrics causing unexpected rapid scale-up during peak batch workloads - Postmortem
creator: Diego Morales
description: During a high-throughput batch export on a customer-dedicated pool we observed large, repeated autoscaler scale-ups over a 90-minute window. The behavior resulted from a recent relabeling change in our metrics pipeline which accidentally exposed batch-processing internal queue depth as the primary KEDA scaler metric for inference workers. The scaler interpreted the batch spikes as sustained request pressure and triggered aggressive scale-ups followed by flapping as the batch drains completed. This postmortem documents the timeline, root cause analysis, impact, and concrete remediation actions to prevent recurrence.
incident_summary: At ~2025-02-14 09:03 UTC multiple Dedicated clusters experienced 3–6x scale-ups within minutes. The autoscaler increased replica counts aggressively; many replicas were short-lived because the underlying load was ephemeral batch flushes rather than sustained inference traffic. Result: elevated cost, transient availability noise (retries/backoffs), and a brief violation of the 99th pctl latency SLO for some customers on dedicated pools.
timeline: 2025-02-14 08:58 UTC - Scheduled batch job triggered in customer environment (large export).
2025-02-14 09:03 UTC - KEDA scaler observed increased 'queue_depth' metric and initiated first scale-up (x2).
2025-02-14 09:05 UTC - Subsequent batch microbursts caused additional scale-ups; replica churn increased and kube events show rapid provisioning/termination.
2025-02-14 09:20 UTC - Alerts: cost anomalies and increased 99th pctl latency for the dedicated cluster. On-call paged.
2025-02-14 09:35 UTC - Investigation: Prometheus relabel rules changed two hours earlier (deploy by ENG-33456). Relabeling accidentally applied to batch job metrics stream.
2025-02-14 09:50 UTC - Temporary mitigation: revert relabel change and apply a KEDA scaler annotation to ignore 'batch_export' job label as a source metric.
2025-02-14 10:10 UTC - Traffic normalized; replicas scaled back to expected baseline. Postmortem triage and assignment begun.
root_cause: A Prometheus relabel rule introduced in a metrics pipeline PR caused an internal batch queue metric to be exposed with the same metric name and labels that the KEDA scaler uses for real-time inference queue length. KEDA's scaler had no validation to differentiate ephemeral batch spikes from steady user traffic, and our cooldown/configuration allowed rapid scale-up without a sustained evaluation window. Combined with the autoscaler's minimal stabilization window, short-lived worker provisioning led to churn and cost impact.
impact: Financial: short-term 3–4x increased GPU provisioning cost for affected clusters over ~90 minutes
Reliability: transient SLO breach on 99th pctl latency for some endpoints; increased retries observed
Operational: on-call time ~2.5 hours for investigation and remediation
Customer experience: one customer reported increased latency for background inference jobs; no data loss or security exposure detected
action_items: ENG-38978: Add metric provenance tagging — ensure relabeled metrics carry origin labels (owner/job) and reject collisions (owner: Diego Morales, estimate: 3, due: 2025-03-07)

ENG-38979: Implement scaler-side metric validation heuristics (ignore metrics tagged as 'batch' or >X variance) and add minimum sample window before scaling up (owner: Ava Chen, estimate: 5, due: 2025-03-14)
ENG-38980: Increase default scale-up stabilization window in KEDA adapter for dedicated pools and make it configurable per pool type (owner: Runtime team, estimate: 3, due: 2025-03-10)

ENG-38981: Add a 'rapid-scale' circuit-breaker that enforces exponential cooldowns and max-replicas-per-duration to limit cost impact from misclassified metrics (owner: Autoscaler team, estimate: 5, due: 2025-03-21)
ENG-38982: Create dashboard and alert for 'metric-origin conflicts' and anomalous label churn in Prometheus relabel logs (owner: Observability, estimate: 2, due: 2025-03-03)
ENG-38983: Run chaos tests simulating batch job bursts to validate autoscaler behavior in staging and add to CI gating for relabel rule PRs (owner: SRE, estimate: 8, due: 2025-04-01)
follow_up_notes: We accepted temporary mitigations (revert + ignore annotation) to stop the immediate impact. Long-term fixes focus on metric provenance and scaler-side protections so relabel failures cannot escalate to production cost/regression. Owners were assigned and all items entered the autoscaling-resilience project. We will validate completed items via a dedicated smoke test and a 72-hour monitoring window post-rollout.
